title: wtm project config
description: Schema for .wtm/config.toml — per-project settings versioned with the repo.

base_path.description: Directory where worktrees are created, relative to the project root. Defaults to ../.trees.

base_branch.description: Default base branch for new worktrees. Usually `main` or `master`.

strategy.description: How .env files are provisioned in new worktrees. example = copy .env.example as .env; main = copy from the main checkout; parent = copy from the source worktree (--from), fall back to main.

file.description: Detected env value files and their committed templates. Each entry pins a value target to the schema template it derives from.

target.description: The .env value file to provision, relative to the project root (e.g. .env, apps/api/.env, .env.local).

template.description: The committed schema template this value derives from (e.g. .env.example). Empty when the file has no template.

local.description: Marks a machine-local override (.env.local). Informational only — it stays syncable.

on_create.description: Commands to run after a worktree is created. Entries can be a plain string or a table {cmd, cwd, continue_on_error}.

oneOf.description: Shell command to run in the new worktree.

cwd.description: Working directory relative to the worktree root.

continue_on_error.description: If true, a non-zero exit doesn't abort subsequent hooks.

on_clean.description: Commands to run right before a worktree is removed (e.g. tearing down external resources like Docker). Entries can be a plain string or a table {cmd, cwd, continue_on_error}. A non-zero exit aborts the removal unless continue_on_error is set.

oneOf.description: Shell command to run in the worktree before removal.

cwd.description: Working directory relative to the worktree root.

continue_on_error.description: If true, a non-zero exit doesn't abort subsequent hooks or the removal.

remembered.description: Answers the wizard no longer asks in this repository, written by its "Always use this answer" toggle. They apply under --yes too; an explicit flag still wins, and --ask asks them again.

env_strategy.description: The env strategy create and checkout use without asking.

isolation.description: The isolation create, checkout and extract give a new worktree without asking.

source_update.description: Whether a source branch behind origin is fast-forwarded (ff) or kept as-is (keep), without asking.
